name: Binary Tree
description: Test your knowledge of tree structures, traversals, and properties.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of height h (where height of a single node is 0)?
questions.explain: The sum of nodes in a perfect binary tree is a geometric series resulting in 2^(h+1) - 1.

questions.question: In which traversal is the root node visited last?
questions.explain: Post-order traversal follows the Left-Right-Root sequence.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of searching for a value in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explain: Balanced trees ensure height is logarithmic relative to the number of nodes.

questions.question: Which type of tree has every node having at most two children?
questions.explain: By definition, a binary tree restricts each node to a maximum of two children.

questions.question: In an in-order traversal of a Binary Search Tree, the values are visited in:
questions.explain: In-order traversal of a BST visits nodes in non-decreasing order.

questions.question: A tree where the height of the two child subtrees of any node differs by at most one is called:
questions.explain: AVL trees are height-balanced binary search trees.

questions.question: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?
questions.explain: The height of a complete binary tree is approximately log base 2 of n.

questions.question: Which traversal is equivalent to a Breadth-First Search (BFS)?
questions.explain: Level-order traversal visits nodes level by level, similar to BFS.

questions.question: In a full binary tree, if there are n internal nodes, how many leaf nodes are there?
questions.explain: In a full binary tree, the number of leaves is always one more than the number of internal nodes.

questions.question: Which property is violated if a node has three children?
questions.explain: A binary tree is strictly limited to a maximum of two children per node.
